extracted.intended_audience: Searle Scholar awardees and recipient institution administrators (research administrators/grant managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and conditions for administration and allowable uses of the Searle Scholars Program $300,000 grant awarded to institutions for a scholar's research over a three-year period. Covers payment schedule, allowable charges, salary rules, intellectual property, and publication acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant amount and payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program provides institutions with a grant of $300,000 for the support of the Searle Scholar’s research during the three-year grant period. Funding for each of the three years will be $100,000, with the first year payable in late June and future payments in September.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant is paid to the institution over three years in annual installments; administration must follow the timing and amounts specified and the grant is subject to the conditions outlined in the Terms of Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on indirect costs / facilities & administrative charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds provided under this grant may not be used to pay costs associated with general facilities or administrative overhead, such as costs of providing space, utilities, library facilities, and administrative services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not charge F&A/indirect costs or general institutional overhead to the Searle Scholars award; budgeting should exclude these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholar salary -- discouraged and conditional approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program does not recommend that Funds be used to support a Scholar’s salary. If the Scholar chooses to allocate a portion of the Award to their salary, said Scholar must email or mail a request to the Program’s scientific director justifying the allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal justification and prior communication to the Program's scientific director is required before allocating any portion of the award to the Scholar's salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholar salary cap
rubrics_metrics.description: In no event may the sum of the salaries and benefits charged for the Scholar exceed $25,000 in any grant fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with approval, scholar salary+benefits charged to the award are capped at $25,000 per year; plan budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries for other project personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries, wages, and benefits may be charged for other individuals working on the Searle Scholars Program funded research project in proportion to the effort expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensate non-faculty project staff from the award according to documented effort; charges should be proportional to actual effort on the funded project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on charging faculty-level salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries may not be charged for others with faculty level appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not charge the award for salary support of other faculty-level personnel; funding is intended for non-faculty personnel and project costs, subject to other stated limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention is made, wholly or in part, with support received from the Searle Scholars Program, the Program shall be notified promptly by email or mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly notify the Program when covered inventions arise; follow institutional patent policies for disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent disposition and licensing income use
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of patents shall be in accordance with the policies of the grantee institution. However, any net income from licensing and royalties shall be divided so that a proportionate amount, which would otherwise accrue to the Searle Scholars Program, shall be set aside and used for the support of biomedical research at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional patent policies govern ownership/disposition, but licensing/royalty income must be apportioned so that the Program's proportionate share is retained within the institution for biomedical research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Should publications result from research so supported, the Searle Scholars Program shall be cited as providing financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit acknowledgement/citation of Searle Scholars Program funding in all resulting publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Terms of Award
rubrics_metrics.description: This grant is subject to the conditions outlined in the Terms of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and institutions must follow the full Terms of Award (referenced by the Program) in administering the grant; the FAQ points to those binding conditions.
